body_text:
Canvas: Frank's bedroom — evening (scene_franks_bedroom_evening) | Node: Frank's bedroom — evening




She walks the hallway slow. The boards she knows the squeak of from the wrong side, the runner Diana picked out three summers ago, the bathroom door closed and dark. The door at the end is the door she's only ever walked past.

It's open by an inch. Lamp light on the floorboards. She pushes it the rest of the way and steps in.

Frank in the chair by the window. He's not undressed. Just sitting in the way he sits — weight on one elbow, the lamp catching the side of his face, a paperback open in his lap that he hasn't been reading. He sets it down on the nightstand without marking the page.

Frank: Close the door.

She closes it. The latch clicks soft. The room is small the way the office is small but it isn't the office — there's no desk between them. Just the bed turned back and the lamp on and Frank standing now from the chair.

💭 Frank is thinking: She came.
Frank: Come here.
Cross to him.







Stay through. Sleep here.
Back to my room before Diana wakes.

body_text:
Canvas: Frank's bedroom — evening (scene_franks_bedroom_evening) | Node: Frank's bedroom — evening




She walks the hallway slow. The boards she knows the squeak of from the wrong side, the runner Diana picked out three summers ago, the bathroom door closed and dark. The door at the end is the door she's only ever walked past.

It's open by an inch. Lamp light on the floorboards. She pushes it the rest of the way and steps in.

Frank in the chair by the window. He's not undressed. Just sitting in the way he sits — weight on one elbow, the lamp catching the side of his face, a paperback open in his lap that he hasn't been reading. He sets it down on the nightstand without marking the page.

Frank: Close the door.

She closes it. The latch clicks soft. The room is small the way the office is small but it isn't the office — there's no desk between them. Just the bed turned back and the lamp on and Frank standing now from the chair.

💭 Frank is thinking: She came.
Frank: Come here.

Two words. The wall on his right is the one Diana's room shares. Maya knows it without having to look — the angle the bed sits, the way the lamp would throw shadow if it were brighter, the boards under her feet that don't squeak anymore because Frank's already on them, crossing to her.

His hand on the back of her neck. Brief. Then his other hand on her hip and he's walking her backwards to the bed without speaking.

Frank: Quiet.

Always the same word. He sits her on the edge of the bed and stands over her for a long second with his hand at her jaw, looking down at her, the lamp behind him so his face is half dark. Then he kneels and pushes her skirt up and his mouth finds the inside of her thigh and stays there, and the only sound in the room is her breath catching and the wall on his right being the wall it is.

Later — the lamp still on, the cover pulled half back, his weight beside her in a bed that is not the desk and not the office and not pretending — he says it again, softer, almost to himself.

Frank: Quiet.

She doesn't answer. The clock somewhere down the hallway clicks over to a new hour.









Stay through. Sleep here.
Back to my room before Diana wakes.
